title: SpaceX Makes History by Catching Giant Rocket
subtitle: The successful return of the Starship spacecraft marks a major step toward future missions to the Moon and Mars.

summary.en: SpaceX successfully caught its Starship spacecraft using large mechanical arms at the launch site. This achievement marks a significant step toward making space travel cheaper and more frequent. While the main spacecraft landed safely, the rocket's booster did not return as planned. NASA is closely watching these tests to support future astronaut missions to the Moon. SpaceX continues to work toward its long-term goal of building a city on Mars.
summary.zh: SpaceX 成功利用發射場的大型機械手臂攔截了星艦太空船。這項成就標誌著太空旅行邁向更低成本與更頻繁的重要一步。雖然主太空船安全著陸，但火箭的推進器並未如預期般回收。NASA 正密切關注這些測試，以支持未來太空人登月的任務。SpaceX 則持續朝向在火星建立城市的長期目標邁進。

paragraphs.en: SpaceX has reached a major goal in space travel. On a recent Saturday, the company successfully caught its massive Starship spacecraft as it returned to Earth. The spacecraft was caught in midair by giant mechanical arms at the same location where it began its journey 22 hours earlier. This event was a major success for Elon Musk and his team, who have been working to make rockets that can be used many times, similar to airplanes.
paragraphs.zh: 太空探索科技公司（SpaceX）在太空旅行領域達成了一項重大目標。在最近的一個週六，該公司成功攔截了其巨大的星艦（Starship）太空船返回地球的過程。這艘太空船在距離起飛地點僅二十二小時後，於原發射場被巨大的機械手臂在半空中接住。這場活動對伊隆·馬斯克（Elon Musk）及其團隊而言是一次重大的成功，他們一直致力於研發能像飛機一樣多次重複使用的火箭。

paragraphs.en: According to NPR News, the mission was a mix of success and challenge. While the Starship spacecraft returned safely, the first-stage booster—the part of the rocket that provides the initial power to leave Earth—did not have the same luck. Shortly after launching from Texas on Friday, the booster experienced problems and ended up in the Gulf of Mexico. SpaceX officials explained that the booster’s engines stopped working too early during its return. The guidance system, which controls the rocket's path, realized it was not in the right position and started a process to destroy the booster to keep the area safe. Engineers are currently looking into exactly what went wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 根據美國國家公共廣播電台（NPR News）報導，這次任務喜憂參半。雖然星艦太空船安全返回，但第一級推進器（即提供離開地球初始動力的火箭部分）卻沒那麼幸運。週五從德州發射後不久，推進器便出現問題，最終墜入墨西哥灣。SpaceX 官員解釋，推進器的引擎在返回過程中過早停止運作。負責控制火箭路徑的導航系統偵測到位置偏差，隨即啟動程序將推進器銷毀以確保區域安全。工程師目前正在調查具體的故障原因。

paragraphs.en: Despite the issue with the booster, the main spacecraft performed very well. It separated from the booster and traveled into orbit, which is the path objects take around the Earth. Once there, it released 26 advanced Starlink satellites. The spacecraft circled the Earth 14 times, which is much longer than previous missions. NPR News reported that the spacecraft’s heat shield, which protects it from the high heat of re-entering the atmosphere, worked exactly as it should have. This flight was the 15th time SpaceX has tested a full-scale Starship since 2023.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管推進器出現問題，主太空船的表現卻相當優異。它與推進器分離後進入軌道，即物體繞行地球的路徑。抵達軌道後，它釋放了二十六枚先進的星鏈（Starlink）衛星。該太空船繞行地球十四圈，飛行時間遠超以往的任務。NPR News 報導指出，用於抵禦重返大氣層高溫的隔熱罩運作完全符合預期。這是 SpaceX 自二零二三年以來，第十五次測試全尺寸星艦。

paragraphs.en: This technology is very important for the future of space exploration. NASA, the American space agency, is paying billions of dollars to use Starship for its Artemis program. The goal of this program is to return astronauts to the Moon later this decade. NASA plans to use Starship to help build a permanent base on the lunar surface. For Elon Musk, the ambitions are even larger. He hopes to eventually use a fleet of these rockets to transport people and supplies to Mars to build a city there. By proving that the spacecraft can be caught and reused, SpaceX is showing that these long-distance trips could one day become a reality.
paragraphs.zh: 這項技術對未來太空探索至關重要。美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）正投入數十億美元，計畫在阿提米絲（Artemis）計畫中使用星艦。該計畫的目標是在本十年末將太空人送回月球。NASA 計畫利用星艦協助在月球表面建立永久基地。對馬斯克而言，他的野心更為宏大。他希望最終能利用這類火箭組成的艦隊，將人員與物資運往火星並在那裡建立城市。透過證明太空船可以被回收並重複使用，SpaceX 正展現出這些長途旅行終有一天可能成為現實。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the company is preparing for more tests. SpaceX expects to start launching Starships from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida within the next few months. This location will be the starting point for future NASA missions. The next big step for the Artemis program involves astronauts practicing how to dock their capsule with a Starship in orbit. NASA is working with both SpaceX and another company, Blue Origin, to deliver crews to the Moon. The agency is currently aiming for 2028 to complete the first human Moon landing since the Apollo era, which ended more than 50 years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，該公司正準備進行更多測試。SpaceX 預計在未來幾個月內，開始從位於佛羅里達州的甘迺迪太空中心（Kennedy Space Center）發射星艦。該地點將成為未來 NASA 任務的起點。阿提米絲計畫的下一個重大步驟，涉及太空人練習如何在軌道上將他們的太空艙與星艦對接。NASA 正與 SpaceX 及另一家公司藍色起源（Blue Origin）合作，將組員送往月球。該署目前目標是在二零二八年完成自阿波羅（Apollo）時代結束五十多年以來的首次載人登月任務。

paragraphs.en: The successful catch of the Starship spacecraft is a big moment for the space industry. It proves that the company’s complex plan for full reusability is possible. While the loss of the booster shows that there is still work to be done, the ability to catch the upper-stage spacecraft is a huge leap forward. As SpaceX continues to refine its technology, the world will be watching to see how these massive machines change our ability to travel beyond Earth. With more flights planned and NASA’s support, the dream of regular travel to the Moon and beyond seems closer than ever before.
paragraphs.zh: 成功攔截星艦太空船是太空產業的一個重要時刻。這證明了該公司關於完全重複使用的複雜計畫是可行的。雖然推進器的損失顯示仍有改進空間，但能攔截上層太空船已是一大躍進。隨著 SpaceX 持續精進其技術，全球都在關注這些巨大的機器將如何改變我們前往地球之外的能力。隨著更多飛行計畫的排定以及 NASA 的支持，前往月球及更遠之處的定期旅行夢想，似乎比以往任何時候都更接近現實。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To intercept and hold something that is moving through the air.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 接住、捕捉（移動中的物體）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於「被抓到（犯錯）」或「趕上（公車）」，這裡指物理上的接住物體。文中：The spacecraft was caught in midair by giant mechanical arms at the same location where it began its journey 22 hours earlier.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To investigate or examine the facts about a problem or situation.
keyTerms.noteZh: look 意為「看」，但加上 into 後變成調查的意思。文中：Engineers are currently looking into exactly what went wrong.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A group of vehicles or aircraft operating together or under the same ownership.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常與海軍（艦隊）連結，在此指 SpaceX 擁有的多艘火箭。文中：He hopes to eventually use a fleet of these rockets to transport people and supplies to Mars to build a city there.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To improve something by making small changes.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常指提煉（如石油），這裡指技術上的持續優化。文中：As SpaceX continues to refine its technology, the world will be watching to see how these massive machines change our ability to travel beyond Earth.

quiz.question: What specifically happened to the first-stage booster during the mission?

options.A: It was successfully caught by mechanical arms along with the spacecraft.
options.B: It was intentionally destroyed after its engines failed to perform correctly.
options.C: It landed safely in the Gulf of Mexico after separating from the spacecraft.
options.D: It successfully delivered 26 satellites into orbit before returning to Earth.

quiz.explanationZh: 根據文章第二段，第一級推進器（booster）因引擎過早停止運作，導航系統判定位置錯誤，為了安全起見啟動了銷毀程序，最終落入墨西哥灣。選項 A 錯誤，因為只有太空船被機械手臂捕捉。選項 C 錯誤，因為它並非「安全降落」，而是因故障被銷毀。選項 D 錯誤，因為衛星是由太空船釋放的，而非推進器。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why is the 'catch' of the Starship spacecraft considered a significant milestone for SpaceX's long-term goals?

options.A: It proves that the rocket can travel to Mars without needing to refuel.
options.B: It confirms that SpaceX no longer needs to work with NASA or other agencies.
options.C: It demonstrates the feasibility of full reusability, which is essential for affordable long-distance space travel.
options.D: It shows that the heat shield technology is now perfect and requires no further testing.

quiz.explanationZh: 文章第一段與最後一段提到，SpaceX 的目標是讓火箭像飛機一樣重複使用。透過成功捕捉太空船，證實了「完全可重複使用」的複雜計畫是可行的，這對於降低成本、實現載人前往火星或月球等長途旅行至關重要。選項 A 文中未提及。選項 B 錯誤，因為 SpaceX 仍與 NASA 密切合作。選項 D 錯誤，文中僅提到隔熱罩運作正常，並未說它已完美無缺無需測試。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'refine' mean as used in the context of SpaceX's technology?

options.A: To improve something by making small changes.
options.B: To define something in a very clear way.
options.C: To discard old technology and start from scratch.
options.D: To increase the speed of production for mass manufacturing.

quiz.explanationZh: 在文章最後一段中，提到 SpaceX 正在「refine」其技術。在此情境下，refine 指的是透過不斷的測試與修正來「改良」或「精進」現有技術，使其更成熟。選項 B 錯誤，定義詞彙不是此處的語意。選項 C 錯誤，refine 是在現有基礎上調整，而非丟棄。選項 D 錯誤，雖然產量可能增加，但 refine 的核心意義是品質與技術的優化，而非單純的生產速度。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the recent SpaceX mission?

options.A: The mission was a complete failure due to the loss of the first-stage booster.
options.B: SpaceX has successfully replaced NASA as the primary leader in lunar exploration.
options.C: The mission was a perfect success with no technical issues encountered.
options.D: Despite some technical setbacks, the mission represents a major advancement in the goal of reusable space travel.

quiz.explanationZh: 文章整體論述重點在於 SpaceX 最近的任務雖然發生了推進器損毀的技術挫折，但成功捕捉太空船是一項重大成就，證實了重複使用技術的可行性，這對未來月球與火星探索至關重要。選項 A 過於悲觀，忽略了任務的成功面。選項 B 錯誤，文中提到 SpaceX 是與 NASA 合作。選項 C 錯誤，文中明確指出推進器發生了問題，並非完美。
